newsitem.title: USA: High Plains Wheat - Basis firm, slow movement.
newsitem.headline: High Plains Wheat - Basis firm, slow movement.

text.p: Basis bids for cash hard red winter wheat in the High Plains were steady to a touch higher on Monday with farmers awaiting higher prices but expiration of free 30-day harvest storage was looming.

Dealers said mill demand remained mostly quiet except for some inquiry from eastern mills. But with 30-day storage contracts beginning to run out after the recent harvest, farmer sales could pick up with a rally in futures, they said.
"Farmer selling due to the storage contracts might make movement a bit more than the market would warrant this week," said one dealer in Hutchinson, Kan.

Dealers noted weakness in Sunday night's CBOT Project A values. Egypt's purhcase of at least 200,000 tonnes of U.S. SRW wheat on Sunday was seen as supportive, but that effect was diluted by scattered rains in Australia at the weekend.
But concerns about another El Nino drought this season in the southern hemisphere remain a factor, dealers said.
The Gulf basis remained steady over the weekend.
Dealers said the market would watch for news of disease problems in spring wheat from this week's crop tour in the Dakotas and Minnesota.
Weekend rains in Kansas, Nebraska and Iowa could help dampen gains in the corn market, removing that support from wheat, some dealers noted.
Basis values in cents/bu against KCBT wheat, cash=dollars/bu.
(Note: N=KCBT July. unq- unquoted, na - not applicable)
